subject: Executive summary: Business metrics, risks, and procurement cues from Fri call
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@healthvera.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@healthvera.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Executive summary: Business metrics, risks, and procurement cues from Fri call

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the candid discussion. Below is a concise recap for your exec team to confirm, plus the next steps Redwood will take to keep momentum.

High-level business outcomes discussed
- Top priority: reduce inference cost on the consumer-facing routing feature (current spend volatility impacting GTM). Target: ~35–45% unit cost reduction over pilot to justify expansion.
- Performance: aim for P95 latency < 120ms in the primary region (US-West) for the 1–2k qps peak pattern you shared.
- Product outcome: improving session completion rate and retention in the flagship app by reducing tail latency and timeouts.

Primary pain/risk items (what you told us)
- Sporadic latency spikes tied to concurrent long-context requests and bursty traffic.
- Procurement constraints: limited procurement cycle and strict redlines around data residency and model usage.
- Compliance ask: audit-log retention and encryption-at-rest key control (HSM/KMS).

What Redwood proposes for the pilot (summary)
- 6-week dedicated pilot on a small reserved pool (dedicated) in your VPC region with a Redwood-managed control plane. Includes KV-prefix caching and optimized batching rules tuned to your request distribution.
- Deliverables: baseline performance/cost report, 2-week optimization pass with quantization/backfill strategy, and a final business-case report for C-suite.
- Success criteria: measured unit cost delta >= 35% and P95 < 120ms at the target qps while preserving output quality on eval prompt set.

Procurement/contract items we flagged today
- Need: SOC 2 Type II evidence + attestation of audit-logs retention policy (we shared baseline in attachments).
- Data residency clause: pilot data must remain in the customer VPC/region; discuss encryption key custody (you prefer customer-managed KMS).
- Usage and IP: we need clarity on model artifacts access — HealthVera prefers no model weights export; Redwood proposes telemetry only for service health (no training data usage).

Attachments (for your review)
- Redwood-POC-Proposal.pdf (pilot scope + pricing assumptions)
- Redwood-Security-FAQ.pdf (SOC2, KMS patterns, audit logs)

Asks / next steps
1) Jordan/Priya: confirm the business outcomes and success criteria above or note edits by EOD Mon (May 18).
2) HealthVera legal: flag must-have contract exceptions (data residency, KMS) so we can produce a contract strawman.
3) Redwood: Karthik and Ben will produce a preliminary SOW and cost estimate by next Friday (May 22).

Notes for internal team (Ben/Karthik)
- Be prepared to propose a Dedicated pilot SKU and an alternate hosted fallback.
- Cost sensitivity: include an option that shows both reserved commitment and on-demand burst.

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a calendar invite for a 30-min legal touchpoint if you confirm.

—
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
hannah.schmitt@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0121
[Attachment: Redwood-POC-Proposal.pdf (pdf)]
[Attachment: Redwood-Security-FAQ.pdf (pdf)]

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@healthvera.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya.desai@healthvera.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Executive summary: Business metrics, risks, and procurement cues from Fri call

Thanks Hannah — helpful recap. Confirming priorities and a few clarifications from our side: 

Confirmed
- Cost reduction target: 35%+ is aligned with expectations to keep the broader rollout in the FY27 plan.
- Latency: P95 < 120ms is the hard constraint for our user-critical path.

Open items (HealthVera)
- Legal: we need a draft clause that explicitly restricts Redwood from using any request payloads for model training or downstream model improvements.
- Data residency: pilot data must remain in our AWS account/region; any telemetry needs explicit allowlist.
- Fallbacks: we prefer an automatic failover plan that preserves availability vs. best-effort degraded performance.

Procurement timing
- Proposed internal schedule: pilot kickoff week of 6 Jul, pilot completes mid-August, procurement and contract signed by early September (target). If Redwood can deliver an SOW + contract strawman by May 22, that keeps us on track.

Attached our constraints doc for procurement (legal will use it as a baseline).

I’ll bring this to my CTO and legal this afternoon — expect edits primarily around the training/data language.

Jordan
Jordan Lee
VP, Product & Engineering | HealthVera
jordan.lee@healthvera.com | +1 (650) 999-4422
[Attachment: HealthVera-Procurement-Constraints.pdf (pdf)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@healthvera.com>, Priya Desai <priya.desai@healthvera.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Executive summary: Business metrics, risks, and procurement cues from Fri call

Appreciate the summary, Hannah. Quick internal notes and commitments: 

Internal plan (short)
- Redwood will model a dedicated-reserved pilot (small pool) and include an alternate hosted fallback plan in the SOW.
- I’ll own the pilot configuration: batch rules, prefix caching, KV limits, and the first quantization pass.
- Ben — can you schedule the pilot kickoff and loop Solutions Eng for test-plan creation? We should also gate a short quality eval on the eval prompt set Jordan shared.

Contract / legal asks
- Legal: we will propose explicit telemetry allowlist language and a non-training clause (no model updates with customer prompt data). Ben/Legal should coordinate to prepare minimal exceptions.

Pricing note
- I’ll circulate a 3-option pricing sheet: (1) reserved pilot (2) reserved + burst (3) hosted pilot with higher unit cost. Expect a first pass by Tue (May 19).

—
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 May 2026 16:20:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: next actions & escalation path for HealthVera opportunity (HV-2026-0423)

Internal follow-up — capturing owners and escalation triggers so leadership has a clear path if procurement gets stuck. Keep this internal.

Owners and near-term deliverables
- Karthik: 3-option pricing sheet and pilot SOW draft — due Tue, May 19 (calendar invite sent).
- Ben: schedule pilot kickoff and Solutions Eng resourcing; draft legal touchpoint invite for next week.
- Hannah: compile SOC2 evidence packet and drive the contract strawman with Legal.

Escalation triggers (if any of these occur escalate to Sales leadership)
- Procurement requests non-negotiable model export or training access.
- Legal requires more than 60 days to finalize exceptions that block a Sept procurement target.
- Business outcome delta: pilot shows < 15% cost improvement after optimization pass (we should pause and reassess).

Next internal checkpoint: Wed, May 20 at 9:00 PT (30 mins) to review SOW + pricing and finalize the legal ask.

—
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
